issues.legal_issue: A dedication of property to an idol is absolute where the instrument, read as a whole, makes the idol the beneficiary and gives sevayats only a limited right to reside there for worship.
material_facts: The will dedicated the property to the idol as its permanent habitation and separately dedicated other land to meet worship and festival expenses.
The will required the property to be registered in the idol’s name, excluded the testator’s heirs and representatives from any interest or right in it, and prohibited its sale or mortgage.
The sevayats were permitted to reside in the property for the purpose of performing the idol’s worship and festivals.
issues.conclusion: The property was absolutely dedicated to the idol; the sevayats’ limited right to reside there for worship did not make the dedication partial.
issues.legal_principle: Whether the idol or the heirs are the true beneficiaries must be determined from a conspectus of the entire instrument: Pande Har Narayan v. Surja Kunwari. A sevayat’s right to reside in a dwelling set apart for the idol, when connected with performing the sevayat’s duties, does not detract from an absolute dedication: Gnanendra Nath Das v. Surendra Nath Das. No statutory provision is relied on for this issue.

rule.if: dedication_dispute and property_set_apart_for_idol and heirs_excluded_from_property and sevayat_residence_limited_to_worship

predicates.dedication_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether property was dedicated to an idol absolutely or only subject to a charge.
predicates.property_set_apart_for_idol: The instrument sets apart the property for the idol, including as its habitation.
predicates.heirs_excluded_from_property: The instrument excludes the founder’s heirs or representatives from interests or rights in the property.
predicates.sevayat_residence_limited_to_worship: The instrument permits sevayats to reside in the property for the purpose of carrying out worship or related religious duties.

issues.definition: When a dedication dispute concerns property set apart for the idol, the heirs are excluded from it, and the sevayats’ residence is limited to worship, the dedication is absolute.

issues.legal_issue: A sevayat cannot acquire title to property dedicated to an idol by adverse possession while holding the property in the capacity of sevayat, and a claimant deriving title from the sevayat’s dealings cannot rely on those dealings to establish such adverse possession.
material_facts: The will provided that the founder’s descendants would successively perform the seva.
The court found that the person who later claimed exclusive entitlement to the property acted as a sevayat and held possession referable to the idol’s ownership.
That person claimed the property as his own after an award, dealt with it, and the appellants later derived title through an auction sale relating to those dealings.
issues.conclusion: The sevayat’s possession and dealings could not constitute adverse possession against the idol, and the appellants did not acquire title by adverse possession through the auction sale.
issues.legal_principle: The possession of a sevayat is the possession of the idol, and a sevayat cannot, while continuing as sevayat, claim adverse possession against the idol. The Court approved the reasoning in Surendrakrishna Ray v. Shree Shree Ishwar Bhubaneshwari Thakurani, which explains that the idol can act through its sevayat and that the sevayat’s change of intention cannot, in these circumstances, extinguish the idol’s right. No statutory provision is relied on for this issue.

predicates.endowment_title_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to title or possession of property dedicated to an idol.
predicates.possessor_is_shebait: The person whose possession is relied on acts as the idol’s sevayat or shebait.
predicates.possession_referable_to_idol: The person holds the property in a capacity or manner referable to the idol’s ownership.
predicates.claimant_derives_title_from_shebait_deal: The claimant relies on a transfer or other dealing with the property made by a sevayat or shebait.

issues.definition: In an endowment title dispute, adverse title against the idol is not acquired when possession is held as sevayat on the idol’s behalf or the claimant derives title from the sevayat’s dealings.
